[Carbon_New_2040 > Emissions Reduction Targets]
Coforge is a fast-growing IT services firm, and the business has grown over 100% in the past 4 years.
The growth in the business has led to an increase in headcount and operations across the globe. As an
organisation, we acknowledge that this could lead to increase in absolute emissions, directly
proportionate to the increase in headcount and business operations. However, as an organisation, we
are committed to assessing our carbon emissions and target to have zero carbon emissions by 2040.
We aim to achieve our target by taking active steps through carbon sequestration and use of renewable
energy technologies, such as solar.

**India location** – Since FY24, when the baseline emissions were assessed, there has been a
continuous focus on emission reduction and focused interventions to ensure that the scope of
emissions is controlled despite the growth of our business operations. Several of our pilot carbon
reduction initiatives were conducted in our India operations.

**International locations (including the UK) –** In 2022, we conducted emission assessment for all
international business operations, including the UK. We are looking to undertake multiple initiatives to
control these emissions, such as reducing the need for air-travel where possible, given that it is a
significant contributor to our emissions for international locations. We are continually assessing our
operations for consolidation of resources to reduce the negative impact on the environment.

[Carbon_New_2040 > Carbon Reduction Initiatives]
In alignment with our goal to be “net-zero by 2040”, we have undertaken the following initiatives and
are actively integrating carbon reduction plans in our global operations:

1.
Coforge has obtained certain global certifications that allow us to reduce our overall carbon

emissions across our operations:

- Environment, Health, and Safety Management System has been implemented in
conformance to ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 standards.

- Coforge owns USGBC (US Green Building Council)-rated Platinum green campuses.
2. We are committed to the utilization of clean fuel and a transition to renewable energy in our

operations. This covers a wide variety of our operations, including transportation, cafeteria
operations and electricity consumption.

- 100% conversion of company cabs and buses to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG).

Introduce electric vehicle fleets (for employees’ transport system) and target 10%
integration by 2028 and ~50% by 2032.

- 100% utilization of Piped Natural Gas (PNG) in cafeteria operations.

- Procure 10% green energy, contributing to total energy consumption by 2025 and
achieve ~ 50% by 2030.

- Support transition to 100% renewable energy by 2040 by committing to the RE100
global initiative. Through this, we pledge to have 100% of our electricity sourced from
renewable sources.

- Engage in community programs to generate renewable energy.
3. Coforge has also committed to interventions with relation to sustainable building and energy

management initiatives in our operations. We have undertaken several pilot initiatives at our
main campus in India, including the following:

- Passive solar architecture for provision of natural day lighting in the building.

Use of double-glazed, high efficiency reflective glass to reduce the solar heat gain by
8% to 10%.

- Rooftop solar energy generation system of 75 KWp and solar-based external area
lighting systems to reduce the consumption of power grid.

Sensor-based lighting system to optimize energy efficiency.

Use of low embodied building material in construction, i.e., fly ash bricks, to reduce
the overall carbon footprint of the building.

- Use of LEDs as replacement of T-5 and LCDs to reduce electricity consumption.

- Solar water heating system in cafeteria.
4. We aim to improve employee engagement and awareness on sustainability and energy

efficiency. We are taking the following steps for the same:

- Conduct one mandatory and two voluntary training sessions annually for all employees to
foster a culture of sustainability.

- Empower employees with knowledge and skills to implement energy-saving practices and
reduce carbon footprint through education and incentive programs.

Coforge has already implemented several of these carbon reduction initiatives at our India locations
and is actively integrating these in our UK operations as well. In addition to the above initiatives, at UK
premise, Coforge adheres with Waste Electrical and Electronic Equipment (WEEE) compliance
standards, which ensures that Coforge responsibly manages electronic waste, promotes recycling,
and follows proper disposal methods for electronic equipment, thus reducing its carbon footprint and
environmental impact.

[Carbon_New_2040 > Declaration and Sign Off]
This Carbon Reduction Plan has been completed in accordance with PPN 06/21 and associated
guidance and reporting standard for Carbon Reduction Plans. Emissions have been reported and
recorded in accordance with the published reporting standard for Carbon Reduction Plans and the
GHG Reporting Protocol corporate standard and uses the appropriate Government emission
conversion factors for greenhouse gas company reporting.

Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions have been reported in accordance with SECR requirements, and the
required subset of Scope 3 emissions have been reported in accordance with the published reporting
standard for Carbon Reduction Plans and the Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Standard.

This Carbon Reduction Plan has been reviewed and signed off by the board of directors (or equivalent
management body).

[Carbon_New_2040 > Signed on behalf of the Supplier]
**John Speight**

President and Head of Europe (EVP)

[Envi_2040-1 > Environmental Sustainability Policy]
**Review Date –** 10 [th] March 2026
**Last Review** – 1 [st] April 2025

© 2026 Coforge

[Envi_2040-1 > Contents]
© 2026 Coforge

[Envi_2040-1 > Scope]
To foster sustainable business development, Coforge is committed to incorporate environmentally conscious practices
amongst all its employees, extended workforce as well as along the supply chain, to whatever extent possible.

This Policy will remain applicable to all facilities and locations of Coforge (rented/ leased or owned) and the
employees and other stakeholders associated with them.

Coforge will also extend the applicability of this Policy across the value chain, to whatever extent possible. All thirdparty associates of Coforge, including suppliers, contractors, vendors, and affiliates, are expected and encouraged to
comply to this Policy.

[Envi_2040-1 > Purpose]
Coforge Limited (hereafter referred to as “Coforge”) is a global digital services and business solutions provider with
in-depth domain expertise that specializes in selected industry verticals. The company strategy is rooted in providing
capability at scale with focus on emerging technologies, building partnerships, focusing on client centricity, and
creating a sustainable and responsible world. Acknowledging its impact and footprint on environment and natural
resources, the company has developed its ‘Environmental Sustainability Policy’ to address the pressing issues of
Climate Change and Environmental Management for Coforge and its value chain. The policy aims to build trust with
stakeholders, increase operational efficiency, and ensure that all its services are environmentally sound and rendered
in responsible manner.

[Envi_2040-1 > Policy commitment]
At Coforge, we recognize the criticality of being a responsible business and believe in creating value for its
employees, extended workforce, shareholders, investors, vendors, suppliers, customers, and other stakeholders.
Being a responsible company, it is a prerequisite to comply with all applicable legal requirements, but being a
responsible and sustainable company, it is imperative to embed the principles of sustainable development in
company’s core business strategy, operational activities and services offered. Coforge is therefore committed to the
following:

Ensure 100% compliance with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements of the laws of the land,
wherever it operates in.

Establish, track, and monitor environmental goals and targets to ensure compliance and performance of the
company with timelines.

Disclose accurate and adequate environmental information based on scientific evidence and data trails for
stakeholder review of company’s performance.

Reduce Coforge’s Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions and carbon footprint generated from business operations
by adopting energy efficient technologies and moving towards renewable energy sources, as applicable.

Implement sustainable waste management practices, based on principle of circularity, i.e., 3Rs (reduce,
recycle, and reuse) especially for food, plastic, and other recyclable/ bio-degradable waste to minimize waste

to landfill.

Drive responsible management of water through conservation, harvesting, and recycling of wastewater,
respectively for reducing consumption of fresh water and reusing of recycled water within the premises.

Environmental awareness training and education for our employees, alongside effective communication with
employees and recognition of their initiatives and achievements towards environmental improvement.

Undertake independent environmental auditing, verification, and certification of our operations, practices and
along our supply chain, as applicable.

Integration of ESG/Sustainability compliances and parameters as part of registration, onboarding, review, and
supplier development processes for all major suppliers as applicable. Periodic vendor/supplier assessment for

© 2026 Coforge

the identified critical suppliers will be conducted covering aspects related to environmental and social
compliances and performance.

Drive capacity building sessions for our vendors/suppliers to motivate them to adopt environment
sustainability practices and social responsibility in their business strategy and operations, in accordance with
Coforge’s Vendor Code of Conduct.

This Policy clearly defines Coforge’s commitments to carbon neutrality, waste management and water conservation,
and the incorporation of sustainable practices into our overall business operations. These commitments are managed
through set environmental sustainability targets that are applicable across our company.

[Envi_2040-1 > Energy Optimization and Emission Management]
We, at Coforge, are committed to become “Carbon Neutral in our operations by 2040”. In line with this commitment,
we have established a sub-target of continuous reduction of GHG emissions by 5% year-on-year, through adoption of
energy efficient technologies/solutions, optimization of energy usage, increase share of renewable energy to total
energy, and biodiversity conservation initiatives that have a cascading effect on carbon offsets.

We are making steady progress against our goal of reducing carbon emissions through an integrated approach. Some

of our internal commitments are mentioned below:

Procure 10% of electricity from green sources by 2025 and increase the share to ~50% by 2030. Transition
to 100% renewable energy by 2050 by committing to the RE100 initiative.

Increase share of electric vehicles (EVs) in fleet for employee commute to 10% by 2025 and to 50% by 2040.

At Coforge, we conduct annual checks on our equipment and optimize operational processes to minimize energy
wastage and optimize energy efficiency. To increase employee awareness, we conduct one mandatory and two
voluntary training sessions annually, empowering them with adequate knowledge and skills on energy-saving
practices and emission management strategies.

[Envi_2040-1 > Waste Management and Circularity]
Coforge has committed to become “Zero Waste by 2040” by creating an effective waste management ecosystem by
adopting the following sub-targets:

The ‘Zero Food Waste’ commitment at Coforge is achieved through diversion of food waste to composting
practices and feed to livestock to minimize waste to landfill.

The ‘Zero Plastic Waste’ commitment at Coforge is reinforced by eliminating the use of single-use plastic on
our premises and responsible disposal of plastics as per local laws and mandates, i.e., through authorized

vendors.

The ‘Zero Waste to Landfill’ initiative at Coforge is supported by our Scrap/E-Waste Disposal Policy,
responsible and scientific disposal of hazardous waste generated and proper recycling of non-food waste
through authorized recycler vendors.

We, at Coforge, are committed to improve resource use through the implementation of the Scrap/E-waste disposal
policy, which aims to reuse and recycle the electronic waste generated by our business operations in a responsible
manner. Through this initiative, the concept of circular economy, i.e., maximizing the reuse and recyclability of
electronic equipment, is promoted, thereby minimizing negative environmental footprint. In addition, we collaborate
with our vendors/suppliers to drive environmental sustainability commitments by prioritizing on minimizing packaging
material consumption and wastage by adopting alternative green solutions/sustainable practices. Coforge commits to
implement a comprehensive digital solution for fleet management and Accounts Payable workflow for invoice
management process which, in turn, drives a paperless work environment in the operations.

© 2026 Coforge

[Envi_2040-1 > Water Management]
Coforge has committed to being “Water Positive by 2040”, a mission that is inclusive of the following standalone sub
targets:

To provide clean drinking water to all employees and extended workforce.

Ensure Water Free Sanitation by 2040, supported by recycling of wastewater and implementation of
sustainable sanitation technologies on our facilities.

To increase non-potable water usage (irrigation and domestic use) to 75% by 2040 from the baseline of 50%
in FY2023, by maximizing wastewater treatment and recyclability to reduce dependency on freshwater.

To enhance the capacity of existing rainwater harvesting systems for all our owned properties, as part of the
company’s water conservation objective.

We, at Coforge, believe in the sustainable management of water resources across our business operations and
facilities, and have developed plans on conservation, harvesting, and recycling of water. Since awareness on water
conservation practices and innovative solutions to maximize water recyclability is of paramount importance for us, we
periodically conduct employee capacity building sessions to drive behavioral change.

[Envi_2040-1 > Environmental Management System]
Coforge is committed to implementing and continuously improving an Environmental Management System (EMS) to
enhance its environmental performance. The company has obtained ISO 14001 certification, covering 60% of its
operations Pan India, with a plan to achieve 100% coverage by the end of 2025.

[Envi_2040-1 > Climate Change Adaptation]
Coforge acknowledges the importance of climate change adaptation and is committed to assessing physical and
transition climate-related risks across its office locations. We will develop resilience strategies to help with adaptation
and ensuring continuity of our operations in a sustainable way.

[Envi_2040-1 > Decarbonization Strategy]
Coforge plans to develop a decarbonization strategy aligned with the SBTi Net Zero Standard for Scope 1 and Scope
2 emissions. We are committed to reducing GHG emissions in accordance with the SBTi framework, which includes:

Setting science-based targets to ensure our emissions reduction efforts are aligned with the latest climate
science.

- Transparently reporting our progress towards these targets to maintain accountability and build trust with
our stakeholders.

- Collaborating with stakeholders to meet our climate objectives and drive collective action towards a
sustainable future.

We intend to address Scope 3 emissions in the future.

[Envi_2040-1 > Monitoring]
This Environmental Policy will be regularly reviewed and updated as per the requirements of the national and local
laws and regulations, as well as in sync with the international commitments on ESG. The periodic review of the Policy
and the commitments mentioned in the same is entrusted with Coforge’s Environment, Social & Governance (ESG)
Committee which convenes on an annual basis, or as and when required, to carry out the exercise. The commitments
and the targets may be reviewed by the Board on a yearly basis, as per the recommendation of the ESG Committee.

The EHS function shall track and monitor the progress against the laid down targets on a monthly basis and a
quarterly trend analysis report, encompassing energy, emissions, waste and water performance, may be submitted to
the ESG Committee for their review and recommendations.

© 2026 Coforge

[Envi_2040-1 > Compliance Obligations]
All provisions of the Environmental Sustainability Policy are subject to revision in accordance with any modification in
the laws and regulations, business strategic decisions, and structural changes at Coforge.

The ESG Committee reserves the right to modify, add and/or amend any of the provisions of this policy, subject to
approval by the Board.

**Approved by:**

**John Speight**

[Water-Management-Policy > Water Management Policy]
**Review Date –** 10 [th] August 2026

© 2026 Coforge

[Water-Management-Policy > Contents]
© 2026 Coforge

[Water-Management-Policy > Purpose]
Coforge Limited (hereafter referred to as “Coforge”) is a global digital services and business solutions provider with
in-depth domain expertise that specializes in selected industry verticals. The company's strategy is rooted in providing
capability at scale with a focus on emerging technologies, building partnerships, client centricity, and creating a
sustainable and responsible world.

Water is a shared and increasingly stressed natural resource that is critical to communities, ecosystems, and the
continuity of Coforge’ s own operations. While Coforge, as an information technology services organization, is not a
water-intensive business, the company recognizes its responsibility to manage water use across its facilities and value
chain in a manner that is efficient, transparent, and protective of shared water resources, particularly in the waterstressed geographies in which several of its campuses and offices are located.

This Water Policy sets out Coforge's approach to responsible water stewardship. It builds on, and provides greater
specificity to, the water-related commitments already articulated in Coforge's Environmental Sustainability Policy,
including the company's ambition to become “Water Positive by 2040”, and establishes the principles, commitments,
objectives, targets, and governance mechanisms that will guide Coforge in achieving this ambition. Coforge defines
“Water Positive” as replenishing more water than is consumed across owned operations through a combination of
water conservation, recycling, rainwater harvesting, watershed restoration, and community water stewardship

initiatives.

The Policy aims to build trust with stakeholders, strengthen resilience against water-related risks, and ensure that
Coforge's services and facilities are managed in an environmentally sound and responsible manner.

[Water-Management-Policy > Scope]
This Policy applies to all delivery centers of Coforge and to all employees and extended workforce associated with
them, across all geographies in which Coforge operates.

Coforge will also extend the applicability of this Policy across its value chain, to whatever extent possible. All thirdparty associates of Coforge, including suppliers, contractors, vendors, and affiliates, are expected and encouraged to
comply with the principles of this Policy, in line with Coforge's Sustainable Procurement Policy.

This Policy is appropriate to the nature and scale of Coforge's operations and reflects the company's commitment to
fulfilling applicable legal and other water-related obligations, preventing pollution, promoting sustainable water use,
and achieving continual improvement in water performance.

[Water-Management-Policy > Policy Commitment]
At Coforge, we recognize water as a shared and finite resource, and believe in creating value responsibly for our
employees, extended workforce, shareholders, investors, vendors, suppliers, customers, and other stakeholders.
Being a responsible and sustainable company requires embedding the principles of water stewardship into our core
business strategy, operational activities, and services offered.

Coforge is therefore committed to the following:

[Water-Management-Policy > Legal and Regulatory Compliance]
- Ensure 100% compliance with all applicable legal and regulatory requirements relating to water abstraction,
use, discharge, and effluent quality, in every jurisdiction in which Coforge operates.

Align Coforge's water management approach with recognized international frameworks and voluntary
commitments, including the UN Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 6 (Clean Water and
Sanitation) and SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities and Communities), and the GRI 303: Water and Effluents

Standard.

Disclose accurate and adequate water-related information based on scientific evidence and verifiable data
trails to enable stakeholder review of the company's performance.

© 2026 Coforge

[Water-Management-Policy > Responsible Water Use and Conservation]
Drive responsible management of water through conservation and efficient use across all delivery centers of
Coforge, with the objective of reducing freshwater consumption and withdrawal intensity over time.

Prioritize water sourcing based on a hierarchy that favors harvested rainwater, recycled water, and other
sustainable alternative sources before increasing dependence on freshwater sources wherever feasible.

Adopt water-efficient fixtures, low-flow sanitary fittings, smart water metering, and leak-detection systems to
minimize water wastage across owned and significant leased premises.

Over the next two years, Coforge will undertake water balance assessments for major facilities to understand
sources, uses, and losses of water and identify opportunities for reduction and substitution with recycled or

alternative water sources.

Coforge intends to establish and periodically review near-term (3-5 year) and long-term (through 2040) water
conservation targets, aligned with its broader Environmental Sustainability Policy commitments.

[Water-Management-Policy > Water Recycling, Harvesting and Reuse]
Enhance the capacity and coverage of rainwater harvesting systems across all Coforge-owned properties, as
part of the company's water conservation objective.

Operate and maintain Sewage/Effluent Treatment Plants (STPs/ETPs) at applicable owned campuses to treat
wastewater for reuse in non-potable applications such as flushing, irrigation, landscaping, and HVAC/cooling

systems.

Increase the proportion of non-potable water demand met through recycled and treated wastewater,
reducing dependency on freshwater and municipal supply.

- Ensure Water-Free Sanitation, supported by wastewater recycling and sustainable sanitation technologies, in
line with Coforge's 2040 ambition.

[Water-Management-Policy > Water Quality and Pollution Prevention]
Prevent pollution of surface water, groundwater, and other water bodies by adopting a zero-discharge
philosophy wherever applicable and technically feasible, and by maintaining water and waste-storage
infrastructure to appropriate technical standards.

Monitor and maintain the quality of water used and discharged at Coforge facilities, ensuring adherence to
applicable regulatory and permit-based discharge standards.

Provide access to clean and safe drinking water to all employees and the extended workforce across Coforge

facilities.

Undertake independent environmental auditing, verification, and certification of water-related practices at
applicable facilities.

[Water-Management-Policy > Value Chain and Supplier Engagement]
Engage proactively with vendors and suppliers to identify and manage water-related risks across the value
chain, in accordance with Coforge's Sustainable Procurement Policy.

- Integrate ESG and water-stewardship considerations into supplier registration, onboarding, review, and
development processes for major suppliers, as applicable.

Conduct periodic assessments of identified critical suppliers covering environmental compliance, including
water-related practices and performance.

Drive capacity-building sessions for vendors and suppliers to encourage the adoption of water conservation
and stewardship practices in their own operations.

© 2026 Coforge

[Water-Management-Policy > Community Water Stewardship]
Recognize that Coforge's operations affect, and are affected by, water availability in the communities in which
it is present and engage with these communities on water matters that are important to them, pursuant to
Coforge's CSR & ESG Policy.

- Support community-level water stewardship initiatives, including wetland restoration and waterbody
rejuvenation projects. Through partnerships with government agencies and implementation partners, Coforge
seeks to contribute to wastewater treatment, groundwater recharge, biodiversity enhancement, and improved
water quality within local communities. Coforge also intends to conduct water awareness and literacy

initiatives in the future.

- Collaborate, where relevant, with local authorities, civil society organizations, and industry bodies to advocate
for and participate in waterbody restoration projects.

[Water-Management-Policy > Awareness and Capacity Building]
Conduct environmental awareness training and education for employees on water conservation practices and
innovative solutions to maximize water recyclability, alongside effective communication and recognition of
employee-led initiatives.

- Promote employee awareness on responsible water use and conservation through sustainability
communications, engagement campaigns, and training initiatives as Coforge's water management program

evolves.

Coforge integrates water conservation topics into its employee awareness and sustainability training

programs.

[Water-Management-Policy > Water Risk Assessment]
Coforge recognizes that water-related risk, including physical scarcity, flooding, declining water quality, and
regulatory change, varies significantly by geography and can affect business continuity, cost of operations, and the
communities in which Coforge's facilities are located:

Coforge will undertake periodic water risk assessments across its facility portfolio, using recognized tools such
as the WRI Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas or the WWF Water Risk Filter, to identify facilities located in waterstressed or high-risk river basins.

Outcomes of these assessments will inform site-level water management strategies, business continuity
planning, and prioritization of conservation, harvesting, and recycling investments.

Water-related physical and transition risks will be considered as part of Coforge's broader climate change
adaptation and resilience planning, in line with the company's Environmental Sustainability Policy.

[Water-Management-Policy > Monitoring, Reporting and Disclosure]
This Water Policy will be regularly reviewed and updated in line with the requirements of national and local laws and
regulations, as well as evolving international ESG commitments.

The Facilities/Administration function will track and monitor progress against the targets set out in Section 4
periodically.

A quarterly trend analysis report, encompassing water performance alongside energy, emissions, and waste
performance, will be submitted to the ESG Committee for review and recommendation, consistent with
Coforge's existing Environmental Sustainability Policy monitoring cadence.

Coforge's water performance will be disclosed annually through the Sustainability Report, prepared in
reference to the GRI Standards, and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) filed pursuant
to SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

Where applicable, Coforge's water-related disclosures will be subject to independent third-party assurance,
consistent with the assurance approach adopted for the company's broader sustainability reporting.

[Water-Management-Policy > Grievance Mechanism]
Coforge provides a transparent grievance mechanism that enables employees, extended workforce, and other
stakeholders to raise concerns relating to water use, water quality, or non-compliance with this Policy. Complaints
may be raised through Coforge's established Whistleblower channel or through the applicable local grievance

redressal mechanism.

All complaints will be handled confidentially, with timely acknowledgment, investigation, and resolution, and in a
manner that ensures non-retaliation against the person raising the concern.

[Water-Management-Policy > Alignment with Frameworks and Standards]
This Policy supports Coforge's alignment with, and contribution to, the following frameworks and standards:

- ISO 14001:2015 – Environmental Management System.

GRI 303: Water and Effluents – Global Reporting Initiative Sustainability Reporting Standards.

- Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) under SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015.

- United Nations Global Compact CEO Water Mandate (as applicable, on the company's continued commitment
to responsible water stewardship).

- United Nations Sustainable Development Goals: SDG 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation) and SDG 11 (Sustainable
Cities and Communities).
